Definition: of Hebrew origin (H7227 with pronominal suffix); my master, i.e Rabbi, as an official title of honor:--Master, Rabbi.
BiblicalUsage: Rabbi, where dwellest thou, asked the two disciples who followed Jesus, and Nicodemus came by night calling Him Rabbi, a teacher come from God. The Pharisees loved greetings in the markets and to be called of men, Rabbi, Rabbi, but Jesus said, be not ye called Rabbi, for one is your Master, even Christ, and all ye are brethren.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the title is the test: men love to be called Master, but Christ will not share the chair. There is one Master in the house of God, and the moment a teacher takes the title for himself he has stopped teaching Christ. I hold that every true teacher points away from himself to the one Rabbi who is worthy of the name.
